html:
Saxony was a German state on the upper Elbe, ruled from Dresden by the Wettin family. On the map from 1783 to 1815 it is the Electorate of Saxony, one of the princes who chose the emperor of the Holy Roman Empire, and from 1806 a kingdom.

Its electors had protected Martin Luther at Wittenberg, which made Saxony the first great Lutheran state. Elector Augustus the Strong also became king of Poland and Lithuania in 1697 and filled Dresden with baroque palaces and art.

In 1806 Saxony sided with Napoleon, joined the Confederation of the Rhine and became a kingdom. It stayed loyal too long. After the Battle of Leipzig in 1813 its king was taken prisoner, and at the Congress of Vienna Saxony lost the northern part of its land to Prussia. The smaller kingdom joined the German Empire in 1871 and became a republic in 1918.
